# External check — FMUCD work orders

**Generated by:** `python -m research.fmucd score`

Agreement between each strategy's severity and the band the organisation's own priority code maps to (`research/external/fmucd_mapping.json`, frozen before sampling). Recorded priority encodes scheduling policy as much as severity, so this is an agreement study, not an accuracy test.

Sample: 300 unplanned work orders (HIGH 100, LOW 100, MEDIUM 100) from 4 universities; input guard passed 19.9% of mapped work orders.

Mapping rationale per university: 2: self-describing codes; 3-CALENDARED, 5-PM CRITICAL and 10-CAL CRITICAL dropped as scheduling bands; 3: self-describing codes; 3-EXPEDITED dropped because this site has no routine band and 'expedited' is not a low-urgency label; 7: codes carry both a name and a response-time target; Scheduled EOM, Scheduled 60 Day and P7 - Seasonal dropped as planned work; 9: self-describing codes, same scheme as university 2

## 2b. Few-shot: the same models with this site's own labelled examples in the prompt

Each work order is judged with 15–20 labelled work orders from its own university appended to the production system prompt (analysis plan section H; examples drawn outside the evaluated sample). Difference = few-shot − zero-shot on the same work orders, 95% cluster-bootstrap CI over universities, unadjusted sign-flip p.

Difference and CI are over the 300 work orders (resampling universities); the sign-flip p is over the four university means, so it cannot go below 0.125.

| Arm | Zero-shot | Few-shot | Difference [95% CI] | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemini_2_5_flash__production | 35.0% | 43.0% | +8.0 [+4, +10] | 0.375 |
| gemini_2_5_flash_nothink__production | 33.3% | 40.7% | +7.3 [+5, +10] | 0.250 |
| gemini_3_5_flash__production | 32.7% | 43.7% | +11.0 [+7, +16] | 0.250 |
| gemma3_4b__production | 36.7% | 38.7% | +2.0 [-1, +3] | 0.500 |
| gpt_oss_120b__production | 32.7% | 35.0% | +2.3 [-5, +8] | 0.750 |
| llama3_2_3b__production | 38.3% | 32.0% | -6.3 [-11, +1] | 0.875 |
| qwen3_4b__production | 35.7% | 42.0% | +6.3 [+0, +23] | 0.500 |
| qwen3_8_27b__production | 34.3% | 36.7% | +2.3 [-3, +14] | 1.000 |

## 3. Upper bound: classifiers trained on this data's own labels

Trained on mapped work orders disjoint from the sample (same universities and filters), tested on the same 300. Shows how much of the recorded band is predictable from the text at all.

| Model | Training work orders | Agreement | Quadratic kappa |
|---|---|---|---|
| tfidf_logreg_fmucd_trained | 6,000 | 68.7% | 0.60 |
| bge_m3_logreg_fmucd_trained | 6,000 | 61.3% | 0.54 |

The gap between this and every arm in section 1 is the finding: the priority band is learnable from the text, but it encodes each site's own conventions, which neither a general language model nor a classifier trained elsewhere can infer.
